en:
I bet it would. Thanks for teaching me all of that stuff
today, Akari-chan.
Hey, no need to be so formal. That's what friends are for, right?
Hehe. Right.

Hehe. Well, I guess I'd better get going. Good luck with
everything!

(That dance battle was a lot of fun... Okay, I guess I'd
better get back to the office.)

Dance battles let you build up your Performance ability much
more easily than you would during work or lessons.

Challenge dancers on the street and improve your skills for
the Princess League finals!

View the rules and controls by pressing <Action:Button_Options@Princess_League> during a
dance battle.
Huh? Aren't you Sawamura-san?
Oh! Yes, um...

Akari. Akari Natsukawa. I'm in the class next to yours at
school. Don't you remember me?
Oh, we're in the same home ec class...

I'm sorry. I don't know many people at school yet. I'm
having a hard enough time just remembering the kids in my own class.

I know how you feel. We both transferred in for high school,
and they've all been together since middle school.

And we're not from Kansai, either, so it's hard to get into
their rhythm.
Oh, you're not from Kansai, either?

Nah. I'm from Tokyo. We just moved to Osaka this year
because of my father's job.
I've been noticing you at school.

You look like you're having a hard time fitting in, and
you're usually by yourself.

It's my own fault, though. I can't seem to work up the
courage to talk to my classmates much.

It's not your fault. I mean, Kansai kids talk really fast.
It makes chiming in kinda hard, ya know?

And I'm sure everybody in your class is shy around you. You
know, holding back a little.
Well, you are in the entertainment business!

You have this special aura about you. I think that makes it
hard for the other kids to approach you.
But I'm really just a regular girl!

I'm from Tokyo, so you and I have the same slower pace. It's
easy for us to talk.
I think so, too, Natsukawa-san.
Just call me Akari. Can I call you Haruka, Sawamura-san?
Sure!
Here's to the two latecomers, then!

You must be tired, going to school and working all the time.
If you ever need somebody to talk to, I'm here.
Okay. Thanks.
Uh-oh! I'm supposed to be at dance practice right now!
Oh, you're studying dance?

Well, nothing all that formal. What I do is more like street
dancing...
I find people dancing around town and practice with them.
Wow! You must be pretty assertive, Akari-chan.

Well, I can't take lessons like you do, so I have to do what
I can on my own, right?
You really love to dance, don't you?
I do! I want to be a choreographer someday.

I want to teach pop idols like you super-cool moves and
dance along with them. Wouldn't that be great?

That's why I'm putting so much effort into my own dancing
now.
And Sotenbori's a major hotspot for dance, so it's perfect.
It is? I didn't know that.

Mhm. I heard Osaka is where break dancing was first
introduced into Japan.

People come here from all over the country in the hopes of
making it as a dancer. Didn't you know that?

I didn't. But I did notice there were a lot of people
dancing on the street.

We all get together and have dance battles. The competition
helps us hone our skills, you know?

Yeah. Two people dance to the same music and compete for the
best performance.

It's a lot more interesting than taking lessons at a dance
studio, and harder too, I bet!
You're probably right.

Hey, I know! Why don't you try one out? You could go up
against me!
What!? Me?
Sure! Why not? You'd love street dancing! It's loads of fun!
And it'd be great practice, too!
Oh, come on! Give it a try!
Wouldn't it be nice to do something fun with a friend for a change?
...Yeah. Okay, I'll do it!

I've never done it before, though, so I might make lots of
mistakes...

Don't worry about that! I'll be there to help you through
it! Come on!
All righty, shall we head out?
You're really giving it your all every day, aren't you?

This is all so new to me, I have to work even harder if I
want to catch up.

But you've only been taking lessons⑬or been in this
industry at all⑬for about six months, right?

And you still managed to win your way to the finals of the
Princess League. That's pretty amazin', if you ask me!

Park-san really knew what she was doing when she signed you.
You've got real talent.

I still have a long way to go, though. Just today alone, I
got yelled at so many times!
But that's very nice of you to say. Thank you, Horie-san.
You're very welcome. Hey, there's that smile I love to see!
By the way, how's school going? Gettin' used to things?
Hmm... I'm not sure.
Not going well?

Well, I'm managing to keep up with my studies. It's just...
I don't have many friends yet.

I see. Yeah, as busy as you are, I don't imagine you have
a whole lot of time to just go hang out, huh?

Exactly. And, well, some of the kids have things to say
about the kind of work I do...
Never mind what kids like that say! They're just jealous!

I try not to let it bother me, but... maybe it is kind of
weird. What I do, I mean.

I think what you and I do gives the audience a chance to
dream.

And speaking as a pop idol fan myself, your performances
are really something special.

I say you should have confidence in yourself! Hold your head
high and proudly proclaim that you're a pop idol!

But truth be told, I get yelled at even more than you do, so
I'm probably not very convincin'.
That's not...

Haruka-chan, I'm still pretty green at this manager thing,
but I'm gonna do everything in my power to support you.
If you ever need anythin' at all, you just let me know!
...Thank you. That's very nice of you, Horie-san.
I really mean it.
Oh, look. We're here.

The Princess League finals start tomorrow! And you've got
work in the morning too, so be sure to get plenty of rest.
Great work today. Good night!
Good night.
All right. Let's head over to Soten TV.
I'll go get us a taxi, and you can catch up with me.

I'll be waitin' for you at the taxi stand. Meet me whenever
you're ready.
Okay. Sounds good.
Let me get straight to the point.

I want the two of you to go to Soten TV right away. It's
about the incident with Manda-san.
I just called and apologized.

Now I want you to go and apologize as well. I managed to set
up a brief appointment with Manda-san.
Yes, of course. Let's go, Haruka-chan.
Haruka, wait.
Come here.
Who taught you how to do your makeup?
I taught myself.
Your foundation is all uneven.
And you don't have on lipstick or anything...
This won't do. I'll have the makeup artist fix you up.
Make sure you learn how to do it competently for next time.
Horie, will you please get the makeup artist?

But, Park-san, if we wait for the makeup artist, won't we be
late to our meeting with Manda-san?
Hmph. I swear, men make the worst managers...
Never mind. I'll fix it myself. You wait outside.

Oh, there you are, Haruka-chan. Let's go in. Park-san's
waiting for us.

So let me get this straight. She has a concert in Tokyo in
just a few days, and you want me to get her ready for it?

Yes. What do you think? With your considerable talents, do
you think you could whip her into shape?
Uh... Is that a "no"?

All I can do for Haruka is point her in the right direction.
I'm sure you understand, Park-san?
Indeed. Thank you.
Huh? I don't...
Haruka is the one dancing. All I can do is teach.
Whether she succeeds or not is up to her.

But I don't think you'll be disappointed. Haruka has amazing
talent.

It's simply incredible how far she's come in only six months
of dancing.
She must have put in extraordinary effort.
So, the time we have left should be more than enough.
I'll leave Haruka in your hands. Thank you.
Okay, I have to head home for today.

We'll start your real lessons tomorrow. I'll come up with a
program for you.
Does that sound all right?
Yes, sir! Thank you very much!

Christina is a true professional who has mastered the art of
dance.

I have complete confidence in leaving everything to him. You
two did very well.
Oh, no, it was nothing. Haha...
Nonsense... That said, today's work isn't over just yet.
Haruka, get changed and come to my office. You too, Horie.
You probably heard, but I just fired Ogita.
Okay. But where does that leave us?

I'm afraid you've already fired just about every dance
instructor in Kansai...

That's why I have a task for the two of you. It would do you
well to listen without interrupting.
Forgive me.

I hear the dance instructor Christina is currently in Japan
for a concert at Osaka Jo Hall.
His full bio hasn't been made public.

But they say there are many stars around the world whose
talent has blossomed thanks to his guidance.
I'm sure you can imagine what I'm going to say next.
Well, uh...

Christina only teaches dancers he's taken a personal
interest in.
Apparently, he's not the type to be swayed by money or power.
So we still have a chance with him.
I want you to find Christina and get him to agree to teach Haruka.

What? Just outta the blue like that? Besides, the Princess
League Finals have already started!
Horie, are you looking to get fired as well?
Oh! No, ma'am! My apologies... I'll do my best.

"Your best"? I don't want you to just do "your best." I want
you to get it done.
Yes, ma'am. I will!
Are we clear, Haruka?
I suggest you start with Sotenbori.

Rumor has it he goes barhopping there alone just about every
night.
In fact, he's likely sitting at one of those bars right now.
All right, Haruka-chan. Let's go find this guy.
Right!
Let's start by seein' what we can find out. We can ask around town.

Oh, hi, Haruka-chan. You're looking for Ogita-san, right?
He's talking with Park-san in her office.

There. See what you can do when you try? Hard to believe you
were a complete amateur just a little while ago.
Don't get too comfy, kid. You're not outta the woods yet.
Next up is your dance lesson.
Ogita-san's waiting for you in the office. Run down and get him, okay?

Haruka! You're late! Round two is gonna start soon, and we
don't have a second to lose!
Sorry, Yamaura-san!
Save it for later. Let's just get started. You ready?
Okay, here we go!
(I'm late. I have to hurry to the lesson studio.)
Oh, there ya are. Welcome back.
Oh, and by the way, Haruka-chan.

I almost forgot to tell you, but I updated your bank book
like you asked.
Oh, I'm so sorry to have put that on you.

Hey, no problem. I crammed your schedule super full, so it's
not like you had time to do it yourself.
Well, thank you for doing that...
(Oh, another bank transfer from Nagasu.)
Is this your idea of hiding from us?
What's up? You look happy.
Hehe, it's a secret.
Okay, well, you got lessons starting at seven.
First up is your voice lesson with Yamaura-san.

Once you've changed in the dressing room, head on up to the
fourth-floor studio like always.
Best of luck!
Being a pop idol sure is hard work...
Just get inside.
I've had complaints from both Manda-san at Soten TV and Osaka Talent.

You were supposed to watch over her! How could you let such
a stupid thing happen!?
I, uh...
I told you to keep her away from the others.
Well, I didn't exactly⑬
I don't want your excuses! Honestly, you're hopeless...!

Listen to me. Haruka doesn't have any naive illusions about
the entertainment industry.

The more she's exposed to the dark underbelly of this
business, the more she's going to see it as just a job.
And I can't have that.

I want her to be able to form her own dream⑬one she can
hang on to.

Some girls need to be taught to grasp the harsher realities.
But Haruka isn't like that.

Haruka needs something she can take with her wherever she
goes!

Don't ever let anything like this happen again. No more
mistakes.
Yes, ma'am. Forgive me.

You did great. There'll be a lot of events like this, so
just keep up the good work.

So, this afternoon is finally the start of the big Princess
League finals.

If you win, you'll make your major label debut with a top
record company.

And on top of that, our agency'll finally make a big splash
in Tokyo!
Apparently, for the finals, you're going to have a simultaneous showdown with your opponent.
Simultaneous?

Yep. You and your opponent will be on stage at the same
time, performin' to the same song.

The one who gets the most fans on their side by the end of
the song wins.
That's a different approach.

Ain't it? You'll be at it for three rounds, and your total
score will determine the overall winner. Ooh, I'm startin'
to get nervous myself!
